outlier: Sidekiq 8.0: Improvements to the Web UI

recent_posts.title: Sidekiq 8.0: Improvements to the Web UI
recent_posts.summary: Sidekiq 8.0 introduces a major overhaul to its Web UI, switching from Bootstrap to vanilla CSS, resulting in a 10x reduction in CSS size and improved performance. Changes include a revised configuration API, internal refactoring for better code understanding and security, and significant performance optimizations. The new Web UI is simpler, faster, and more maintainable.

recent_posts.title: Conventional Commits
recent_posts.summary: Conventional Commits is a standard for writing commit messages that are useful for both humans and machines. The writer describes setting up a Git commit message template to make it easier to remember the standard format. This template includes different categories such as 'feat', 'fix', 'docs', and others, and is integrated into Git configuration for consistent use.

recent_posts.title: Sponsoring Hanami
recent_posts.summary: A $12,000 grant has been awarded to the Hanami framework, aimed at diversifying the Ruby ecosystem, which is heavily centered around Rails. Hanami 2.2 recently shipped with features like database ORM and migration support that prevent the N+1 query problem. The grant aims to support project leader Tim Riley in dedicating more time to Hanami, and it encourages other Ruby-based organizations to contribute to its development.

recent_posts.title: Iteration and Sidekiq 7.3.0
recent_posts.summary: Sidekiq 7.3 introduces Iterable Jobs to address the issue of long-running jobs by breaking them into discrete chunks. The cursor tracks the progress within the sequence, allowing jobs to resume smoothly after interruptions. This version also enhances web security by disabling raw JS code in the Web UI to prevent XSS attacks. Additionally, it allows Sidekiq Enterprise to use Redis Cluster for rate limiters and offers more configurable logging and timeout settings.

recent_posts.title: Redis Licensing Changes and You
recent_posts.summary: Redis has changed its licensing to prevent service providers from adding closed source changes to their Redis service offerings. This change does not affect Sidekiq and Faktory users. Sidekiq is also compatible with multi-threaded forks of Redis.

recent_posts.title: Serializing Ruby datatypes in JSON
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to serialize Ruby datatypes into a JSON document using Ruby's JSON library. Understand the limitations of using non-JSON-native datatypes and discover a feature that allows you to serialize most core datatypes.

recent_posts.title: How does Sidekiq work?
recent_posts.summary: A blog post delves deep into Sidekiq's internals, explaining how it actually works. It is a fantastic resource for learning about Ruby infrastructure and background jobs.

recent_posts.title: How does Sidekiq work?
recent_posts.summary: Sidekiq is a Ruby background job processor that offloads the execution of application logic into the background. It uses a threaded model for job processing and Redis as a backend. It offers additional paid versions - Pro and Enterprise, each with more features and extensions. This article explores the internals of Sidekiq to highlight its key aspects and implementation decisions.

recent_posts.title: Supporting Dragonfly
recent_posts.summary: Dragonfly is a Redis-compatible tool that offers better performance for certain tasks, including multi-core capabilities. It has been tested to handle over 400,000 jobs per second on a 96-core EC2 machine.

recent_posts.title: Ruby HTTP Server from scratch
recent_posts.summary: Mike Perham has added support for Kubernetes HTTP health checks to Sidekiq Enterprise. This means we need to implement an HTTP server which listens on port X and simply returns 200/OK if the process is alive. No need for serving files or arbitrary dynamic content so there's no need for routes, paths or query parameter handling.
